functions.name: batch-enrich-contacts
functions.description: Submit up to 100 contacts in one asynchronous enrichment job, with independently selected email/phone categories per contact. Returns a job ID, not fabricated per-contact successes.

name.description: Readable dashboard name for this enrichment job.

custom.description: At most 20 string-valued correlation entries echoed in results; empty object is retained.

domain.description: Employer domain, not a complete website URL.

items.description: An information category to enrich for this contact.

fields.description: Information categories requested for this contact, with no implicit paid categories.

firstName.description: Contact's given name; empty or missing clues may be skipped only when skipInvalidContacts is true.

professionalNetworkUrl.description: LinkedIn standard or Sales Navigator URL; provider validates identity clues and can skip invalid data when requested.

items.description: Identity clues, requested categories, and optional correlation metadata for one contact.

contacts.description: Contacts to submit in this one job; public maximum 100, provisionally selected for bounded submission.

skipInvalidContacts.description: When true, the provider skips contacts with invalid identity data and returns them without enrichment data; otherwise such data rejects the request.

FunctionInput_fullenrich_batchenrichcont.description: A named asynchronous enrichment job containing 1-100 contacts with independently selected categories.

enrichmentId.description: Opaque identifier of the accepted job; retrieve its status and contact records using get-contact-enrichment.

FunctionOutput_fullenrich_batchenrichcon.description: Job acceptance only; does not indicate completion or individual contact enrichment success.

tags.instructions: Use for 1–100 contacts in one background job; use `enrich-contact` for a single-contact interface. Choose fields per contact and attach custom correlation metadata if needed. By default invalid contact data rejects the request; skipInvalidContacts enables provider skipping. Save enrichmentId and use `get-contact-enrichment` later. Do not replay while a job is pending, and do not interpret acceptance as completed enrichment.

functions.name: batch-reverse-lookup-contacts
functions.description: Submit 1–100 email addresses in one asynchronous reverse-lookup job to identify associated professional profiles.

name.description: Readable dashboard name for this reverse-lookup job.

email.description: Email address to identify, preserving exact spelling; provider validates it so invalid rows can be skipped when requested.

custom.description: At most 10 correlation entries echoed in results, each string value at most 100 characters; empty map is retained.

items.description: An email lookup record with optional correlation metadata.

contacts.description: Email lookup records for one job; maximum 100 is a provisional bounded-submission choice.

skipInvalidContacts.description: When true, contacts with empty or invalid emails are skipped and returned without profiles instead of rejecting the request.

FunctionInput_fullenrich_batchreverseloo.description: One asynchronous reverse-lookup job containing 1–100 email records.

enrichmentId.description: Opaque ID of the accepted asynchronous reverse-email job; not a per-item success acknowledgment.

FunctionOutput_fullenrich_batchreverselo.description: Acknowledgment of an accepted asynchronous reverse-email job, without individual lookup results.

tags.instructions: Use for multiple email-to-profile identifications; use `reverse-lookup-contact` for one address. Maximum 100 records per submission. Use custom metadata to correlate results. By default invalid emails reject the request; skipInvalidContacts permits provider skipping. Save enrichmentId and call `get-contact-reverse-lookup` later. Acceptance does not establish per-email matches, and replay may create duplicate paid work.

functions.name: enrich-contact
functions.description: Submit one contact for asynchronous email and/or phone enrichment and return the enrichment job ID. This starts credit-consuming work; it does not wait for enrichment to finish.

name.description: Readable dashboard job name; defaults to Contact enrichment when omitted.

items.description: Contact information category to search for.

fields.description: Contact information categories to search for; no implicit paid categories are added.

custom.description: Optional correlation metadata echoed by the provider; at most 20 string-valued entries. Empty object is retained.

domain.description: Employer domain, not a full URL.

professionalNetworkUrl.description: LinkedIn standard or Sales Navigator profile URL.

contact.description: Known identity clues for the contact to enrich.

FunctionInput_fullenrich_enrichcontact.description: One known contact and the contact information categories to enrich asynchronously.

enrichmentId.description: Opaque identifier of the accepted asynchronous enrichment job; use with get-contact-enrichment.

FunctionOutput_fullenrich_enrichcontact.description: Acceptance of an asynchronous enrichment job, not its completion or discovered contact information.

tags.instructions: Use to start enrichment for one known contact. Supply a profile URL or name plus employer context, and explicitly choose which contact fields to find. Use `batch-enrich-contacts` for up to 100 contacts. Save enrichmentId and call `get-contact-enrichment` later; do not resubmit simply because processing is unfinished. No emails are sent to the contact.

functions.name: get-company
functions.description: Get a company by its FullEnrich ID, domain, or professional-network identifier. Domain and professional-network lookups return the provider's best match and can consume credits.

domain.description: Company domain, such as anthropic.com, rather than a complete website URL.

companyId.description: Opaque FullEnrich company ID returned by company discovery.

professionalNetworkId.description: Opaque decimal professional-network company identifier; supplied as a string to preserve precision.

FunctionInput_fullenrich_getcompany.description: Exactly one known company identifier to retrieve.

domain.description: Company domain, distinct from its declared website.

logoUrl.description: Provider-hosted company logo URL; may be empty when the profile handle is unknown.

offices.description: Additional offices; preserves null, an empty array, and omission distinctly.

line2.description: Raw full locality/address line; not parsed into geographic fields.

website.description: Declared website URL, including any subdomain, path or tracking parameters; omitted when unavailable.

headcount.description: Reported employee count; zero can coexist with a known employee-count range.

description.description: Company description as ordinary Unicode text.

specialties.description: Company specialties; preserves an explicitly empty array.

yearFounded.description: Founding year; zero is the provider's unknown-year sentinel.

headquarters.description: Structured headquarters; an empty object means no headquarters data was available.

mainIndustry.description: Primary industry category; omitted if unavailable.

id.description: Opaque network profile identifier, represented losslessly as a decimal string.

connectionCount.description: Number of company followers reported by the provider.

company.description: Matching company, or null when no company matches.

creditsConsumed.description: Provider-reported credits consumed by this request; omitted if not reported.

FunctionOutput_fullenrich_getcompany.description: The matching company and any provider-reported credit consumption.

tags.instructions: Use for one known company. Obtain companyId from `list-companies` or `search-companies`, or supply a domain or professional-network identifier you already have. Supply exactly one identifier. Use `search-companies` for discovery. A null company means no match; a result is not proof that the company owns a supplied domain.

functions.name: search-companies
functions.description: Find one page of company profiles using inclusion, exclusion, exact-text and numeric-range criteria. Requests can consume credits.

limit.description: Maximum companies in this page; defaults to 10.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from this search with the same filters; omit for the first page.

field.description: Company attribute to match; keywords searches company descriptions, and headquartersLocations accepts cities, regions or countries.

value.description: Text or opaque FullEnrich ID to match, depending on field.

exclude.description: Exclude matching companies when true; otherwise require a match.

exactMatch.description: Case-insensitive exact stored-value match when true; otherwise tolerate minor text differences.

value.description: Opaque decimal network company identifier, serialized internally as an integer.

exactMatch.description: Provider exact-term matching flag for network IDs; preserves the documented provider behavior rather than text equality.

max.description: Inclusive upper employee count or founding year; omitted for an open upper bound.

min.description: Inclusive lower employee count or founding year; omitted for an open lower bound.

field.description: Inclusive employee-count or calendar founding-year range.

exclude.description: Exclude companies within the range when true.

filters.description: Search criteria; multiple criteria for the same provider field are ANDed. Inclusion and exclusion retain provider semantics.

logoUrl.description: Company logo URL; may be empty when the handle is unknown.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation for unchanged filters; omitted when exhausted.

creditsConsumed.description: Provider-reported credits consumed by this request; omitted if unavailable.

FunctionOutput_fullenrich_searchcompanie.description: One provider-ranked company search page with reported credits and continuation.

tags.instructions: Use for company discovery; use `get-company` for one known company or `list-companies` for unfiltered browsing. Multiple criteria for the same field use AND, not OR. Monthly database updates can change subsequent results even though provider tokens do not expire.
